newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ dairy group to build 350MW power plant - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: NZ dairy group to build 350MW power plant - NZPA.

text.p: New Zealand Dairy Group is today expected to announce plans to build the country's biggest private power station, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.

The proposed plant at Te Rapa near Hamilton will rival the planned Stratford 350MW power project at Taranaki, due to begin production in 1998, for the claim of New Zealand's biggest private energy project.
The giant Hamilton-based dairy company, which has a factory at Te Rapa, was expected to make the announcement early this afternoon, NZPA said.
NZDG chairman John Storey said he would not comment before the announcement.
The plant would generate enough electricity to supply all Waikato's needs for many years, and guarantee the region a secure electricity supply.

NZPA said the plant, close to the Electricity Corporation's Huntly power station, would use coal and or gas to produce steam and hot and chilled water for NZDG's big milk factories. NZDG has coal mines in the Waikato.
A number of major players in the electricity and gas industry are jostling for selection as NZDG's co-generation partner.
They are said to include the country's biggest electricity company Mercury Energy and its Canadian partner TransAlta Energy, Natural Gas Corporation, Contact Energy and Waikato supplier WEL Energy.
